intro: The India e-Arrival card lets visitors complete their arrival card online before they travel. Here’s what it is, who fills it in, and why you should never pay for it.

sections.heading: What is the India e-Arrival card?
sections.text: The e-Arrival card is the online version of the paper landing card. Foreign visitors and OCI cardholders can complete it within 72 hours before arriving in India.

sections.heading: Where do I fill it in?
sections.text: On the Bureau of Immigration website, on indianvisaonline.gov.in, or in the official Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app. It’s free.

sections.heading: Is it a visa?
sections.text: No. You still need your e-Visa or regular visa. The e-Arrival card is extra arrival information. [Read our full guide](/india-e-arrival-card/).

sections.heading: Who fills in the India e-Arrival card?
sections.text: Foreign visitors and OCI cardholders arriving in India. Each traveller needs their own, including children. Have your passport, visa and travel details ready.

sections.heading: Watch out for fake websites
sections.text: Some websites charge for the e-Arrival card. The official service is free, so don’t pay anyone to fill it in for you.

sections.heading: What if I forget?
sections.text: You may be asked to fill in an arrival form when you land, which can mean waiting longer at immigration. Completing it online before you fly saves time.

title: India e-Arrival Card Explained: Who Needs It and Is It Free?
description: India’s e-Arrival card explained: what it is, when to fill it in, where to find the official free form, and why it doesn’t replace a visa.
